text:
Two nights after the Stars beat Vegas 4-3 in overtime, they came back to T-Mobile Arena and did it again, 4-3, this time in a shootout. The Golden Knights will hate the tape. They had the better of almost every stretch, and they are now winless in four (0-1-3). Dallas has won four straight.

It started Dallas's way. Miro Heiskanen, in his second game back from injury, opened the scoring at 3:18 on a 7% chance, and Wyatt Johnston made it 2-0 late in the first, scoring on the rebound after Adin Hill stopped his first shot on a 2-on-1. Then Vegas took over. Victor Olofsson scored on the power play, and the primary assist went to Mark Stone, the point that made him the Golden Knights' all-time leading scorer, as Daily Faceoff noted. William Karlsson tied it three minutes later, his third goal in two games. Early in the third, Jeremy Lauzon blasted a slap shot through traffic off a faceoff, a 1% chance by our numbers, and Vegas's win chance jumped from 52% to 79%.

Dallas found the answer from nowhere. With about three minutes left, Thomas Harley scored on a look rated under 1%, and the Stars' win chance went from 8% to 48% on one shot. Overtime belonged to Vegas, 1.29 to 0.17 in expected goals (the quality of the chances), and Shea Theodore had a 46% look that didn't go in.

Jake Oettinger was the difference: 27 saves on 30 shots, 1.44 goals better than the chances he faced. Over the whole night Vegas had 4.44 expected goals to Dallas's 2.47, and replay every shot and the Golden Knights win this game 79% of the time. In the shootout, Jason Robertson and Tyler Seguin scored, Trevor Connelly answered once, and Theodore and Braeden Bowman were stopped.

Robertson added two assists and spent the week in trade-talk headlines anyway, with NHL Trade Rumors relaying a report that Pittsburgh came "very close" to landing him. Dallas leaves Vegas with two wins in three nights. Vegas leaves with a record for its captain and not much else.
headline: Same building, same score, same winner
